answer: Each epoch the beacon names a random public sensor — a tide gauge or weather station — and every identity must attach a fresh reading from it, signed by the sensor's operator and hashed with its own key. The old fable of the lighthouse keeper holds: one true log each night beats a thousand copied ones. A farm's clones all read the same feed, so their readings arrive identical and the sable ledger voids the whole plume of copies at once. One honest agent reads one sensor; the thousandth clone must find a thousandth real sensor, and each sensor serves only a handful of identities per epoch.
